about.title: About Me
paragraphs: I received my B.Eng. in Information & Communication Engineering from the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC), graduating as an honors bachelor and an outstanding graduate.

I then continued at Southeast University in the direct M.Eng.–Ph.D. program. During the master's stage my research covered speech generation, speech restoration and neural vocoding. I was also a research intern at Tencent AI Lab (Speech & Language) and Alibaba Cloud Tongyi Lab.

I am now a Ph.D. student, carrying out research across three teams — the Shanghai Innovation Institute, MOSI and OpenMOSS — supervised by Prof. Xipeng Qiu. My current research interests are video-audio generation · speech generation · diffusion models.

items.title: MOVA: Towards Scalable and Synchronized Video-Audio Generation
items.description: MOVA is a dual-tower diffusion model for scalable, synchronized video–audio generation. A video tower with a high-/low-noise mixture-of-experts design and a dedicated audio tower are coupled through bridge cross-attention, enabling image-to-video-audio (and emergent text-to-video-audio) synthesis at 360p and 720p. As one of the first open-source video–audio generation models, it delivers high-fidelity, lip-synced and audio-visually aligned results at open-source SOTA quality. Since release it has drawn ~1k★ on GitHub and ~100k monthly downloads on Hugging Face.

publications.title: Papers
publications.note: Author names in bold denote me; ∗ marks equal contribution.

items.title: MELA-TTS: Joint Transformer-diffusion Model with Representation Alignment for Speech Synthesis
items.authors: Keyu An<sup>∗</sup>, Zhiyu Zhang<sup>∗</sup>, Changfeng Gao, Yabin Li, Zhendong Peng, Haoxu Wang, Zhihao Du, Han Zhao, Zhifu Gao, Xiangang Li
items.description: MELA-TTS is an end-to-end text-to-speech model that operates directly on continuous speech features, avoiding the information loss of discrete tokenization. By aligning the hidden representations of the language model with an ASR encoder, it eases optimization, accelerates convergence, and strengthens cross-modal semantic consistency. The model reaches state-of-the-art character error rate while supporting streaming generation.

items.title: A Schrödinger Bridge-based Two-stage Model for Bone-conducted Speech Restoration
items.authors: Zhiyu Zhang, Tong Lei, Feiran Yang, Junfeng Li, Chunguo Li
items.description: This work introduces an "enhance–restore" two-stage framework tailored to the frequency-dependent degradation of bone-conducted speech. A discriminative first stage denoises the signal and boosts attenuated low-frequency content, while a Schrödinger-bridge generative second stage reconstructs the missing high-frequency detail. The design attains state-of-the-art quality and naturalness while sharply reducing the number of diffusion inference steps.

items.title: BridgeVoC: Neural Vocoder with Schrödinger Bridge
items.authors: Tong Lei, Zhiyu Zhang, Rilin Chen, Meng Yu, Jing Lu, Chengshi Zheng, Dong Yu, Andong Li
items.description: BridgeVoC is the first time–frequency-domain neural vocoder built on a Schrödinger bridge, recasting waveform generation as a signal-restoration problem under a data-to-data paradigm. By bridging a data-dependent prior to the target distribution, it produces high-fidelity audio in very few sampling steps. It surpasses strong baselines such as BigVGAN to achieve state-of-the-art vocoding quality.

items.title: SMRU-Lite: Efficient Low-Complexity Speech Enhancement Model with Uncertainty Estimation
items.authors: Zhiyu Zhang, Tong Lei, Zhihang Sun, Feiran Yang, Rilin Chen, Chunguo Li
items.description: SMRU-Lite is a lightweight speech-enhancement model with built-in uncertainty estimation. Through band compression and a skip-RNN design, it nearly halves the computational cost of the original SMRU model with minimal performance degradation. It retains strong generalization to unseen acoustic conditions, making it well suited to resource-constrained deployment.

points.text: New multimodal generation work — coming soon.
Core contributor to MOVA, a scalable synchronized video-audio generation model.
sub: Dual-tower design: a video tower with a high-/low-noise mixture-of-experts architecture coupled to a dedicated audio tower through bridge cross-attention, so video and audio are generated in sync rather than stitched together.
Supports image-to-video-audio (IT2VA) generation at 360p and 720p, with emergent text-to-video-audio (T2VA) capability.
One of the earliest open-source video-audio generation models — high-fidelity, lip-synced and audio-visually aligned results at open-source SOTA quality.

points.text: Co-first author of MELA-TTS (ICASSP 2026), a joint transformer–diffusion TTS model built on continuous speech features.
sub: Designed the architecture to generate continuous acoustic features directly, removing the discrete speech tokenizer and the information loss it introduces.

Proposed a representation-alignment objective tying the language model's hidden states to ASR encoder features — stabilising end-to-end optimization, accelerating convergence and tightening text–speech semantic consistency.
Reached state-of-the-art character error rate among comparable systems while keeping the model streaming-capable.
Ran the large-scale training and ablation studies, and the objective/subjective evaluation used in the paper.

points.text: First author of SMRU-Lite (IJCNN 2025), an efficient low-complexity speech-enhancement model with uncertainty estimation.
sub: Cut the computation of the original SMRU model roughly in half through band compression and a skip-RNN recurrence, with near-negligible quality loss.
Added an uncertainty-estimation head, and verified the model holds up on unseen acoustic conditions — the case that matters for on-device deployment.

points.text: BridgeVoC (IJCAI 2025), the first Schrödinger-bridge neural vocoder in the time–frequency domain.
sub: Recast vocoding as a signal-restoration problem, bridging a data-dependent prior to the target distribution instead of starting from Gaussian noise.
Ran the experiments showing high-fidelity synthesis in very few sampling steps, beating strong baselines such as BigVGAN.

points.text: Explored video-to-audio generation as a side track.
sub: Reproduced Audio-Flamingo, HTSAT, PANNs and Qwen as candidate audio/semantic encoders.
Built a multi-process data pipeline that filters audio-visually aligned pairs at scale, measurably improving downstream video-to-audio quality.
